| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | This is an APA-wide journal policy (not Psychological-Assessment-specific): generative AI may be used for drafting/editing/analysis but must be disclosed in the relevant manuscript section (Method/Introduction/Author Note/Results depending on use); AI cannot be listed as an author; authors remain fully responsible for verifying AI-generated content/citations; confidential submitted content may not be entered into generative AI tools; routine AI-assisted copyediting does not need disclosure. No submission-time checkbox/permission gate described — enforcement is disclosure-based (self-report), hence 'conditional' gate rather than a hard yes/no. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/resources/publishing-tips/policy-generative-ai |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Empirical research on clinical-psychology assessment: development/validation of assessment instruments, scales, structured/observational interview methods; clinical judgment and decision-making research; translational work applying basic psychological science (cognitive, personality-social, biological psychology) to clinical assessment; integrative/systematic reviews of assessment literatures.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** psychometric scale/instrument development and validation, clinical interview and observational assessment methods, measurement invariance / psychometric modeling (IRT, CFA, DIF), clinical judgment and decision-making studies, translational basic-to-clinical assessment research, integrative reviews of assessment domains
